newsitem.title: UK: UK traders see wheat sales to Spain at 450,000 T.
newsitem.headline: UK traders see wheat sales to Spain at 450,000 T.

text.p: British wheat sales to Spain may reach 450,000 tonnes this season (July/June), a large volume considering Spain's ample 1996 harvest, traders said.
A UK trade mission to Spain concluded after a visit last month that British material was still in demand as local farmers kept the market undersupplied in the hope of higher prices.

"Interest in importing British grain remains strong because Spanish farmers are not releasing their grain on to the market and the millers still need low P/L wheat from the UK to blend with their own wheat," the British Cereal Exports (BCE), an arm of the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA), said in a report.
UK wheat exports to Spain were a hefty 906,000 tonnes, mainly non-breadmaking quality, in the 1995/96 season when its own production was hit severly by drought.
"This year they have a much bigger crop," said one HGCA official.
The London-based producer-consumer body International Grains Council (IGC) estimated Spain's total wheat and barley crop at 16.7 million tonnes in 1996, up from just 8.2 million in 1995.

Other European estimates pegged Spain's milling wheat output at 4.2 million tonnes. Barley exports were expected to be worst hit with Spain's home-grown crop estimated to have doubled to over 10 million tonnes. Large offers into intervention is a likely scenario.
"The main problem is barley," said one trader, estimating UK barley sales to Spain at around 50,000 tonnes this season, down from 482,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
Traders said UK exports benefited from competitive prices and lack of aggressive sales by French cooperatives but the situation could reverse if French wheat undercut UK prices.
Traders put total UK wheat exports, mainly non-breadmaking, at 1.290 million tonnes by the end of October.
